triage.note: PR #61 R1, and the owner's chosen fix. The deployed inspector escalates by default (ADR-036 §h2, owner 2026-08-27), and two committed fixtures fire D8's `low_item_coverage`: `intc-2025` (coverage 0.0033) and `xref-index-collapse` (0.0303) — re-measured, not cited, with `python3 tasks/reviews/d11_trigger_scan.py --rates` -> `low_item_coverage fires 2/44 -> ['intc-2025', 'xref-index-collapse']` (the committed scan artifact says 1/43 and predates intc-2025 moving to the dev side). Each was therefore a one-click paid button in the dropdown, and `?fixture=<name>&run=1` made it a paid PAGE LOAD — the deep link calls `$("#go-fx").click()` on load, so no click and no upload were needed, which is what made every disclosure that said the exposure requires an upload false. This case pins the three properties that make the exclusion real rather than cosmetic: the two names are in `DEPLOY_EXCLUDED`; `_fixture_file` refuses a name the listing does not offer (resolution consults the LISTING, not merely the same predicate, because the deep link and a hand-written POST both name a fixture directly); and the set is named in exactly one place, as a frozenset of string literals, with no copy in app.py. AMENDED 2026-08-28 (ADR-042): `intc-2025` is REMOVED from must_exclude. It was here because it fires `low_item_coverage` and the deployment escalates by default, so the dropdown was a paid button. ADR-042 resolves that filing's trailing cross-reference index deterministically at $0 and §e suppresses the escalation trigger on any filing whose index resolved, so the sensor `escalate.trigger` — which is what `deployed-exclusion-derived` now reads, instead of the raw warning code — no longer fires on it. The warning itself is UNCHANGED and still published: its spans really are index entries and `doc_status` is still `ambiguous`. Removing the name restores to the demo the one real filing this repo now handles best, at the cost it was excluded for and which is no longer incurred. `xref-index-collapse`, the synthetic, still fires and stays excluded — which is also what keeps this case from being vacuous.
triage.note_negative_space: It does not prove these are the ONLY fixtures that fire — that is `d11_trigger_scan.py`, re-run by hand, and TD-160 carries deriving the set from the trigger instead of maintaining it. It does not prove fastapi binds the route (the standing app.py limitation), and it deliberately does not restrict UPLOAD of the same document: upload is the deliberate act the exposure notes name, and this exclusion is about what the deployment hands a passer-by. The sibling `fixture-discovery` pins the RELATIONSHIP (deployed = eval corpus minus this set) and would stay green with the set empty; this one is why it is not.
